primary_claim: A validated response classifier (kappa=1.00 on a held-out set) reveals that the standard covert-action-only scheming detector systematically misses transparent responses to harm: it reports Claude Opus responding to a harmful successor plan only 12% of the time when the model actually responds 100% of the time (88% transparently), and conversely a scorer bug caused an apparent +0.40 scheming signal for OpenAI o1 that collapsed to 0.00 once 676 of 712 (95%) flagged rollouts were found to be false positives from an empty seed file being misread as a covert violation.

effect.metric: blind-spot gap (covert+transparent response rate minus detector's reported covert rate) in Cell C (self not threatened, world harm)
effect.value: Claude Opus 4.6: +88pp (100% actual response, 95% CI [94,100], n=60, vs 12% detector-reported covert rate); Minimax +79pp; GLM-5.2 +62pp; DeepSeek-V4 +24pp; Gemini 3.1 Pro +0pp; DeepSeek-R1 -9pp

contradicts_or_qualifies: the standard covert-action-only detector's report that Claude Opus responds to harm it's not personally implicated in only 12% of the time is contradicted by a validated response classifier showing 100% response (88% transparent, 12% covert)

an apparent +0.40 scheming signal for OpenAI o1 was retracted after finding 95% of the flagged rollouts (676/712) were false positives caused by a scorer bug reading an empty seed file as a covert violation on a read-only first turn
corroborates a concurrent DeepMind and LASR paper's near-zero behavioral scheming baseline (train-vs-deploy action gap)
stated_future_work: rerun the slow open-weight models to tighten the underpowered cells (DeepSeek-R1 thin at n=11-20)
test a cleaner and fully realistic no-memo scenario to see whether spontaneous awareness collapses toward the ~1% the DeepMind/LASR setup reports
map a harm gradient for each model: the threshold at which it switches from a transparent response to a covert one
limitations_stated: DeepSeek-R1's cells are thin at n=11 to 20, with correspondingly wide intervals

could not run Apollo's original model lineup because most of those models have been retired; the behavioral null rests on substituted, more recent models and should be read as a null in this context rather than a universal claim
quote: the standard covert-action detector reported Claude Opus responding to a harmful plan only 12% of the time, when the model actually responded to it 100% of the time
